title: Finish In Balance Hold The Pose (Chas McIvor)
style: Country rock with bluegrass influences. Features a prominent banjo playing rapid rolls, a driving acoustic guitar, and a deep, resonant baritone male vocal. The arrangement includes a steady drum kit with a crisp snare and a walking electric bass. A fiddle provides melodic fills and a solo section. The tempo is 115 BPM in 4/4 time, likely in the key of G major. The vocal delivery is rhythmic and instructional, characterized by a Southern drawl. The production is clean with minimal reverb, emphasizing the percussive nature of the banjo and the clarity of the vocal performance. The track features a breakdown section with handclaps and a fiddle solo before returning to the full band arrangement.
lyrics:
[Intro]
[banjo rolls, acoustic guitar strumming, steady drum beat]

[Verse 1]
[baritone male vocals]
I say son, the swing ain't done at impact
Finish in balance, hold the pose, that's a fact
If you can't hold it [drum fill]
You swung too hard!

[Chorus]
[fiddle enters]
Ye-haw!
Weight ninety percent on the lead foot at finish
Trail toe pointing down, hip don't diminish
Belt buckle facing the target for
Chest rotate, eyes follow the pole
Hold the finish three seconds, son, if you wobble or fall you overdid the run
Balance is the report card of the swing
Good swing, good balance, the bell will ring

[Verse 2]
Finish in balance, hold the pose, son
Three second freeze, the work is done
Lead foot ninety, trail toe down
Belt buckle target where the crown of the round

[Bridge]
[bass and drums continue]
Oh, if you fall back you came over the top
If you fall forward you slid through the stop
If you fall after you swung too steep
Diagnose from balance, son, don't weep

[Verse 3]
I say boy, every range session
Finish every swing in balance, the lesson
Hold three seconds every single time
Balance becomes habit, balance becomes prime

[Chorus]
Finish in balance, hold the pose, son
Three second freeze, the work is done
Lead foot ninety, trail toe down
Belt buckle target where the crown of the round

[Breakdown]
[drums and handclaps only]
One, two, three, four!
[fiddle solo with banjo accompaniment]

[Outro]
Hold the pose, three count
Balance shows what the swing recounts
Lead foot loaded, belt buckle through
That's my boy, that's your view
[banjo flourish, final drum hit]
